answer.explanation: A merge conflict happens when Git can’t automatically decide how to combine changes from two branches. Here, both branches changed the same line (`GREETING = ...`), so Git marks the conflict with `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, and `>>>>>>>` to show where the changes diverged. You must edit the file to keep one version or combine them manually, then mark it as resolved with `git add`.

answer.cause: GitHub no longer accepts plain passwords for HTTPS authentication. You need a [personal access token (PAT)](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/managing-your-personal-access-tokens) instead.
answer.explanation: GitHub disabled password-based HTTPS authentication to improve security. Now you must use a personal access token (PAT) as your 'password' when pushing via HTTPS. This token is like a password but is safer because it can be revoked if compromised.

steps.why: Temporarily caches your credentials to avoid re-entering them every time. This is optional but convenient. If you prefer, skip this step.
Go to [GitHub Personal Access Tokens](https://github.com/settings/tokens) in your browser. Log in with your GitHub username and password (not the PAT).

Click **Generate new token** (classic). Give it a descriptive name (e.g., 'Git CLI'). Select the **repo** scope (or more if needed). Do **not** enable 2FA unless you want to. Click **Generate token**. Copy the token immediately—you won’t see it again!
When Git prompts for your password, paste the copied PAT as your password. Your username remains your GitHub username.
Push your changes to GitHub using your PAT. This should now work.

warnings: Never share your PAT with anyone. Treat it like a password.

If you accidentally commit sensitive data (e.g., passwords, tokens) to your repo, you must rotate them immediately. If the repo is already pushed to GitHub, you’ll need to use [GitHub’s secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/about-secret-scanning) or contact GitHub support.
If you lose your PAT, generate a new one and update your cached credentials with `git credential-manager reject https://github.com` (or clear your credential cache manually).
